content: Magnesium hydroxide is a medication that is prescribed for short-term use to treat constipation. It may also be prescribed for other purposes; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Magnesium hydroxide is available in tablet and liquid forms, which are taken orally. It is typically used as needed for constipation. Follow the instructions on the packaging or your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take magnesium hydroxide exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it, or take it more frequently than prescribed by your doctor. If you are using the liquid form, make sure to shake the bottle well before each use. Before taking magnesium hydroxide, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to magnesium hydroxide or any other medications. Additionally, provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are currently taking, including vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have or have ever had kidney disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking magnesium hydroxide, contact your doctor immediately. If you forget to take a dose of magnesium hydroxide, this is usually not an issue since it is taken as needed. However, if your doctor has instructed you to take it regularly, take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Magnesium hydroxide may cause side effects. If you experience any of the following symptoms, contact your doctor immediately: stomach cramps, upset stomach, vomiting, or diarrhea. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor can report it to the Food and Drug Administration's (FDA) MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in the container it came in, ensuring it is tightly closed and kept out of reach of children. Store it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any medication that is expired or no longer needed. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on the proper disposal of unused medication. If you have any questions about taking this medication, ask your pharmacist for clarification.
